attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post. He bases them on TD Cowen's analysis but states the 14% figure as his own conclusion.

semantics.note: The claim keeps 'effectively', the over-14% threshold and the TD Cowen basis as a condition. The denominator is his own 6–7 GW estimate, which the contract correctly flags.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair: abandoned prospective GW divided by operating GW at the time, on a comparable basis. The result depends on the power basis, overlap between agreements, and the estimated denominator.

evidence.note: Dated Bloomberg report of TD Cowen's findings (voided leases of a couple hundred MW, SOQ pullback). It gives no operating-capacity denominator, so it cannot settle the 14% figure.

reviews.rationale: The packet confirms a large abandoned pipeline, as reported by TD Cowen. But it has neither a verified contemporaneous operating-capacity denominator nor the original analyst report with comparable GW figures. The ratio over 14% can't be confirmed or refuted.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: 'Suggests that they're not going to improve' is an inference he hedges, not a firm commitment; the drafter rightly records the modality as 'likely'. 'Mediocre' is a value judgment. Under policy, a hedged forecast is not scored.

contract.note: The contract scores a hedged statement on a plain reading, but plain reading applies only to firm language. It also reads 'improve' as absolute growth in run rate, whereas he may have meant the numbers stay mediocre relative to spending.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own FY26 Q3 disclosure: AI run rate above $37B, well over the $13B baseline. This would count against a firm no-growth reading, but the claim is hedged and so not scored.

reviews.rationale: The forecast rests on 'suggests', an inferential hedge with no firm commitment, and the 'mediocre' part is normative. Under policy, hedged forecasts are not scored, even though the reported AI run rate later rose well above $13B.

attribution.note: Zitron's own summary in his post, after he cites Ars Technica and Karpathy.

semantics.note: 'Appears to be' sits beside 'to be crystal clear', so it reads as softening of an observation he states firmly, not a probability hedge. The three parts (price, modest gains, benchmark deficits) are kept.

contract.note: Comparing API list prices and reading 'modest-at-best' against benchmark gains are ordinary readings. Counting o3-mini as a 'competing model' is a judgment call, and it affects the deficit component.

evidence.note: OpenAI's launch post lists GPT-4.5 at $75/$150 per million tokens and calls the model compute-intensive. This supports the much higher price.
Same-period price comparison with GPT-4o ($2.50/$10): 30x higher for input and 15x for output tokens.

OpenAI's own table shows large gains over GPT-4o on GPQA (+18 pts) and AIME (+27 pts), which counts against 'modest-at-best'. It also shows o3-mini ahead on GPQA, AIME and SWE-Bench, which supports the deficit part.
METR's pre-release checkpoint placed GPT-4.5 between GPT-4o and o1, consistent with OpenAI's results. It used a different checkpoint, so context only.

reviews.rationale: Supported: GPT-4.5 was far more expensive (30x/15x list prices), and an alternative model (o3-mini) beat it on several benchmarks. Contradicted: 'modest-at-best improvements' conflicts with large GPQA and AIME gains over GPT-4o, though some other gains were small. 'Ruinously' is evaluative and not established.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: In context, 'Expansion which' refers to Microsoft's expansion, which the previous sentence describes it as slowing. The normalised claim widens this to data center expansion in general, changing the scope.

contract.note: The contract adopts the industry-wide reading and admits the scope is ambiguous. The speaker's sentence ties necessity to Microsoft's expansion. Since necessity has no period or scale, the result depends on the evaluator's framing.

evidence.note: Chinchilla (2022) shows better performance from the same compute. It predates the claim and does not test sustained growth with unchanged physical capacity.
IEA projects data center electricity demand to double by 2030. A conditional forecast of consumption does not establish that expansion is necessary.

reviews.rationale: No item measures generative-AI capability and deployment growth against an unchanged or growing physical capacity footprint, under either Microsoft-specific or industry-wide scope. The efficiency research and demand projections are only context. Necessity is neither shown nor refuted.
